name: NICE: endometriosis tests in primary care
headline: NICE draft guidance proposes two non-invasive endometriosis tests for NHS primary care
summary: NICE draft guidance proposes that two non-invasive tests for endometriosis could be used in NHS primary care while more evidence is gathered.
keyPoints: NICE draft guidance proposes that two non-invasive diagnostic tests for endometriosis could be used in NHS primary care while more evidence on their accuracy is gathered.
The two tests are Endotest, which analyses a saliva sample, and EndoSure, which measures electrical signals in the gut.
NICE says the average wait for an endometriosis diagnosis is more than nine years.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body: NICE has published draft guidance proposing that two non-invasive diagnostic tests for endometriosis could be used in the NHS in primary care while more evidence on their accuracy is gathered. Endotest analyses a saliva sample for tiny biological markers called microRNAs. EndoSure detects endometriosis by measuring electrical signals in the gut.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: NICE says the average wait for an endometriosis diagnosis is more than nine years. A third test, DotEndo, which is a blood test, is not among the tests in the draft recommendations. Because this is draft guidance, the recommendations may change after consultation.

source.title: New technologies could help cut years-long wait for endometriosis diagnosis, says NICE
